Where it began

Kyle Jamieson was born in Auckland on 30 December 1994. He went to Auckland Grammar School and later studied at Lincoln University. As a teenager he was a point guard in the basketball academy of the New Zealand Breakers, but he was also a quick bowler, and cricket won. He played for New Zealand at the 2014 Under-19 World Cup.

At first he was more of a batting all-rounder. From 2012 he was slowly turned into a bowler under the eye of Dayle Hadlee, the brother of Richard Hadlee, which is a fair place to learn the trade.

The player

At six feet eight inches he was, by November 2026, the tallest man to have played international cricket for New Zealand. He bowled right-arm fast-medium and was useful with the bat lower down. For Canterbury on 1 January 2019 he took 6 for 7 in a Super Smash match, the best T20 figures in New Zealand at the time, and he finished that season as the leading wicket-taker with 22.

The international start was quick. He was Player of the Match on his ODI debut against India in February 2020, made his Test debut against India on 21 February 2020 and took five wickets in an innings in his next Test. In January 2021 he took 11 for 117 in a Test against Pakistan. By November 2026 he had played 21 Tests and taken 90 wickets at 20.23, with six five-wicket innings and a best of 6 for 48.

What made him special

His great day came in the final of the 2019–2021 World Test Championship, which New Zealand won. He took seven wickets in the match, five of them in the first innings, and was named Player of the Match. The ICC put him in its Test Team of the Year for 2021.

He could bat too, with 523 Test runs at 20.92. His only Test fifty ended on 51 not out, which suggests a man who knew exactly when he had done enough.

Away from the middle

He took his game abroad as well, joining Royal Challengers Bangalore in the IPL and Surrey in county cricket in 2021, and he also played for Delhi Capitals. He also took a hat-trick for Canterbury against Central Districts in the Plunket Shield in October 2020, and he was picked for New Zealand at the T20 World Cups of 2021 and 2026.

And finally

He gave up a place at a basketball academy to bowl fast. The Breakers lost a point guard who stood six feet eight, and a good many Test batters spent the next few years wishing he had stayed.
